founderText: Should we charge libraries or students?

response.answer:
Your interviews show students already work around the problem [E1]. What evidence do you have that libraries would pay?

- Separate what you know from what you assume.
- Run a priced test with two libraries.
- Decide on a threshold before you start.

claims.text: Nine of fourteen students walk between buildings to find a seat.
Libraries may value occupancy data more than students value convenience.
Run a priced test with two libraries.

uncertainty.item: Whether any library has a budget for this.

response.challenge: What would convince you that students will never pay?

next_actions.action: Email two library managers with a priced pilot offer.

follow_up_questions: How many library managers have you spoken to so far?

evidence.title: 14 problem interviews with undergraduates
evidence.excerpt: Nine of fourteen students described walking between two or more buildings to find a seat.

evidence.title: Campus Pilot Partnerships Office
evidence.excerpt: Helps student ventures arrange pilots with university departments.
